intro: Move a property tax rate up or down — the town’s, the county’s, or the schools’ — and see what it does to a household’s bill, to the budget, and to what that money could pay for or would have to give up. Every rate and tax base comes from a cited document.

household.homestead_label: It’s my homestead (takes off Florida’s homestead exemption)
household.where: The household example is a home inside the Town of Melbourne Beach (millage code 34X0), so it pays the town, Brevard County, and Brevard Public Schools.
household.note: Florida taxes property on its assessed value, in mills: $1 for every $1,000. Enter your assessed value from your TRIM notice or bcpao.us. The homestead box takes off $51,411 for town and county taxes and $25,000 for school taxes (2026 amounts, per the Property Appraiser); homes assessed under about $76,000 get a smaller exemption, and senior, veteran and other exemptions aren’t modeled. County and school rates are the final 2025 rates — the 2026 table wasn’t posted yet. Smaller taxes on the bill (library, mosquito control, recreation, water management, inlet and navigation districts — 1.1933 mills together in 2025) stay as they are.

layers.name: Town of Melbourne Beach mills
layers.base_note: One mill raises about $725,978 a year — the town’s 2026 taxable value is $725,977,934 (Property Appraiser’s certification). The town budgets 97% of that, since some taxpayers pay early for a discount. The stormwater debt mill ended when that loan was paid off in July 2026.

projects.name: the state-required town hall elevator repair
a year of road paving and curbs

caps.text: Above the rolled-back rate of 4.3987 mills — the rate that would raise the same money as last year — Florida’s Truth in Millage law has the town advertise the rate as a tax increase. FY2027’s 4.6000 is 4.58% above it.
Florida’s Constitution caps city and town operating taxes at 10 mills (Art. VII, §9(b)), not counting voter-approved debt.

layers.name: Brevard County general fund mills
layers.base_note: One mill raises about $76.4 million a year across the whole county — its 2026 taxable value is $76,403,021,129. The county’s general fund pays for the jail and most county services. 2.8643 is the 2025 rate.

caps.text: Florida’s Constitution caps county operating taxes at 10 mills (Art. VII, §9(b)).

layers.name: Brevard Public Schools mills
layers.base_note: One mill raises about $82.9 million a year — the school district’s 2026 taxable value is $82,873,662,940. The 6.31 mills (2025) are 3.062 required by the state, 0.748 set by the School Board, 1.5 for buildings, and 1.0 that voters approved for teacher pay.

caps.text: The state sets the required mills each year; Florida law caps the School Board’s own operating levy (0.748 mills, the amount the state budget allows) and its building levy at 1.5 mills (§1011.71). Anything more needs the voters — as the teacher-pay mill did.

law.text: Florida’s Truth in Millage (TRIM) law: each August the Property Appraiser mails every owner a notice with each government’s proposed rate and its rolled-back rate; budgets are then adopted at two September hearings.
Homesteads get up to $51,411 off town and county taxes in 2026 ($25,000 off school taxes), and Save Our Homes limits a homestead’s yearly assessment increase to 3% or inflation, whichever is less.

On the November 3, 2026 ballot, Amendment 3 would raise the homestead exemption for non-school taxes to up to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, and cut the yearly cap on non-homestead assessment increases from 10% to 5%. School taxes would keep the $25,000 exemption. It needs 60% to pass. In FY2024-25, homesteads paid 59.7% of the town’s property taxes. This site gives facts on the amendment and takes no side.

Also on the ballot: the town’s $5.0 million General Obligation bond, which the town estimates at 0.53–0.70 additional mills a year for 20 years ($131–$175 a year on $250,000 of taxable value). Facts only, no side taken.

limits: Tax bases are held at the 2026 certified values. Values move every year, and if Amendment 3 passes, homestead taxable values would fall sharply starting in 2027.
Not every bill gets paid on time, and early payers get up to a 4% discount; the town budgets 97% of its levy for that reason.
County and school mills raise money from every property in Brevard County, not just homes in Melbourne Beach.
Save Our Homes means a long-time homesteader’s assessed value can be far below market value. Use the assessed value on your notice, not the sale price.
Saving-up times ignore interest earned and rising construction costs.
